//: Which message catalogue each key lives in — the mapping table behind
`scripts/split-locales.mjs`. Longest prefix wins; `shell` is
`locales/en.json` + `locales/hi.json`, which every route downloads; every
other name is `locales/catalogues/<name>.{en,hi}.json`, which only the
screens that import `src/i18n/catalogues/<name>` download.
Two rules sit ABOVE this table, so a line here cannot break a screen:
1. a key the shell's own code references (the root layout, every group
layout, the error and not-found boundaries, and everything they
import) stays in the shell whatever its prefix says — the script
reads the import graph to find them;
2. a key whose prefix is not listed stays in the shell, and the script
says so. New namespaces cost bytes on every route until they get a
line here; they never cost a raw message id on screen.
Other tracks keep adding keys to `locales/en.json` and `locales/hi.json`
as before. Re-running the script moves each one to where this table puts
it; `npm run i18n:check` fails until it has been run.
A sub-prefix gets its own catalogue when a SMALL part of a big namespace is
rendered on screens that do not otherwise need the namespace — payment
modes on the expense, payment and bill screens, say — so those screens
do not download the whole of it for seven words.
